doc.title: Sherrie Maricle interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Why she went on to a doctorate at NYU
summary: Michael Moore suggested NYU; she got a scholarship, a master's and a fellowship, then delayed her dissertation ten years.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: What inspired you to pursue your education all the way through a doctoral degree?

Well this is a — this will sound — it’s not lame but I mean I just wanted to move to New York. I didn’t have any thoughts like — I never even though about going to graduate school, when I was at SUNY Binghamton. There was a concert there with a bassist, Michael Moore was the bass player. And I love the way he played. And my first thought was if I ever get to make a CD I’m going to ask him to play with me, which I did. But I was saying to him, “I’m going to move to New York next year, any hints like what should I do?” And he said, “well I teach at this school, NYU.” I really didn’t, I don’t even think I’d heard of NYU. I’m like oh do they have a music department? He said, “yeah, why don’t you go check it out?” So I called and I went down and I was like that might be an okay way to like slide into New York with just, instead of just going cold. So I auditioned and got in. I really didn’t like it. It was not a strong department, so I was going to leave and just live in New York. And they said, “wait, we’re going to give you a © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-

graduate scholarship.” And then I got my master’s degree and then they hired a new program director and the department started to get better. And then I was done and they said, “we don’t want you to go we’re going to give you a doctoral fellowship.” So when you don’t have any money or a job it’s hard to turn down free school and a little salary. So that’s maybe not the best, I didn’t have like high academic aspirations, so I mean that’s why I finished all my doctoral coursework and I’m embarrassed to say I was my full ten years of not writing my dissertation then had to go into the maximum amount of extensions just because I wouldn’t write it. I just function much better under pressure and deadlines. So I was at the thing where if I didn’t write it my whole class work was going get wiped out. So that’s why I finished it.
Wow. You had to get desperate.
Yeah. I mean because I kept thinking what do I need it for. I didn’t — I’m never a quitter so I knew that I would make myself write it.
